diy: Clean a smelly sink drain: half a cup of baking soda, then a cup of vinegar, wait 15 minutes, flush with hot water.
Remove hard-water stains from taps with a cloth soaked in vinegar wrapped around them for 30 minutes.
Fix a squeaky door hinge with a few drops of coconut oil or a rub of candle wax.
Deodorise the fridge with an open bowl of baking soda; replace every 3 months.
Clean the mixer jar: blend warm water, a drop of dish soap and a pinch of salt for 30 seconds.
Label every switch on your distribution board so you know which breaker is which.
Re-pot one plant and add a layer of compost; money plant and snake plant are hard to kill.
Clean AC filters every 2–4 weeks in summer; it improves cooling and cuts power use.
Use old toothbrushes for grout and tap corners.
Keep a basic toolkit: screwdriver set, tape, pliers, a torch and spare fuses.
Descale the electric kettle by boiling water with a spoon of citric acid or vinegar, then rinse twice.
Microwave a bowl of water with lemon slices for 3 minutes; wipe the steam-softened grime away.
Organise one drawer today: empty, wipe, keep only what you use.
Fix a wobbly chair by tightening screws or adding felt pads under the short leg.
Make an all-purpose cleaner: one part vinegar, one part water, a few drops of lemon (not for marble or granite).
Check smoke alarms (if fitted) and replace batteries twice a year.
Seal gaps under doors with a draught stopper to keep out dust and mosquitoes.
Clean ceiling fans with an old pillowcase so the dust falls inside it.
Store onions and potatoes separately; together they spoil faster.
Rotate the mattress every three months for even wear.
beauty: Apply sunscreen (SPF 30+) every morning, even indoors near windows.
Moisturise within 3 minutes of a shower to lock in moisture.
Change your pillowcase twice a week for clearer skin.
Drink enough water and sleep well; they show on your skin before anything else.
Use lukewarm, not hot, water for your face and hair.
Oil hair (coconut or almond) once a week, an hour before washing.
Exfoliate gently once or twice a week, not daily.
A cold spoon or chilled cucumber slices on the eyes helps morning puffiness.
Remove make-up and sunscreen before sleeping, every night.
Keep nails short and clean; push cuticles back after a shower.
Lip care: a little ghee or lip balm at night stops cracking.
Trim hair every 8–12 weeks to stop split ends travelling up.
Patch-test any new product on your inner arm for 24 hours.
Use a separate towel for your face and wash it often.
Men: shave in the direction of hair growth after a warm shower to reduce bumps.
A simple routine (cleanser, moisturiser, sunscreen) beats ten products used inconsistently.
home_health: Open windows for 10 minutes morning and evening to refresh indoor air.
Wash bedsheets weekly in hot water to reduce dust mites.
Keep a first-aid kit: bandages, antiseptic, thermometer, ORS, paracetamol, and check expiry dates.
Empty standing water in pots and trays weekly to prevent mosquito breeding.
Disinfect phone, remote and door handles weekly.
Keep medicines and cleaning products locked or out of children's reach.
Wash fruit and vegetables under running water before eating.
Store cooked food in the fridge within two hours.
Use a separate chopping board for raw meat and for vegetables.
Replace your toothbrush every three months or after an illness.
Keep emergency numbers (ambulance 108, your doctor, nearest hospital) on the fridge.
Get a water purifier serviced on schedule; change filters as recommended.
Add indoor plants for a calmer space (they help mood more than air quality).
Book an annual health check-up for each adult; put it in the calendar now.
